chunks: He said: Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me from his father who reported from Ahmad ibn Idrees, who reported from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Razi, from ‘Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hurmuzani, who reported from ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali, from his father al-Husayn, peace be upon them, who said:

When Fatimah, the daughter of the Prophet, fell ill, she willed to ‘Ali to withhold the news of her death and treat it as a secret; and to allow no one to visit her during her illness. So he did accordingly, attending on her himself, helped by Asma’ bint ‘Umays, so as to maintain the secrecy as she wished. Then as her death drew near, she willed that Amirul Mu’minin should attend to her rites, to bury her at night and to efface the trace of her grave. So Amirul Mu’minin arranged accordingly, buried her and concealed the place of her burial.

When he dusted off the earth of the grave from his hands, he was so overwhelmed with grief that tears rolled on his cheeks. And then he turned his face towards the grave of the Prophet and said: “Peace be upon you from me, O Messenger of Allah! And peace be upon you from your beloved daughter, the delight of your eye, your visitor, resting in the earth in your locality, for whom Allah so destined that she should join you so soon. O Messenger of Allah, it is indeed difficult to forbear the parting of your beloved daughter and my strength has waned with the demise of the lady who was above the women of the world.

My main source of solace has been from your tradition and from the grief at your departure. For I laid you in the niche of your grave after you breathed your last on my chest, and I closed your eyes with my own hand, and I attended to your rites myself. Yes, and the Book of Allah has the best guide to submission: ‘To Him we belong and unto Him shall we return.’ The trust has thus been returned and the pledge redeemed; and al-Zahra has been snatched away. How ugly has the green sky and the dusty earth become! O Messenger of Allah! As for my sorrow, it is ever lasting, my nights sleepless. The grief cannot leave my heart, till Allah destines for me the same abode as yours. It is the heartache like a festering wound, and the irritating distress. How soon have we been parted from each other! And I raise my complaint to Allah!

Your daughter will inform you how your Ummah rallied against me and worked together to usurp her right. So you seek information from her. How much of ill feeling wrestles within her chest! for which she found no expression. She would say: ‘Allah will judge, and He is the Most Just of the Judges.’

Farewell greetings to you O Messenger of Allah! Not from weariness or seeking respite. If I go, I do not go because of tiredness, and if I stay on, it is not because of any distrust in what Allah has promised the patient ones. And patience is a blessed and more auspicious option. And had it not been for the prevailing authority against us, I would have found a place by your graveside, and would have lived in seclusion near it, and would have wailed the way a bereaved mother wails over her dead son, over the most distressing calamity. With Allah as Witness, your daughter is buried in secrecy, her rights usurped forcefully, and her inheritance denied openly. And the time has not been long, nor had you been forgotten. So, the complaint is raised to Allah, O Messenger of Allah! And to you I offer the most sincere condolence; and the blessing of Allah be upon you and her, and His Mercy and His Grace.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Amirul Mu’minin (Commander of the Faithful) — title of Imam ‘Ali
key_terms.إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون: Istirja‘ — Qur’anic phrase of resignation to God’s will (Q 2:156)
key_terms.الزهراء: al-Zahra (the Radiant One) — title of Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet
key_terms.الوديعة: al-wadi‘a — the trust/deposit, referring to Fatimah as a trust from Allah
key_terms.ملحود: lahd — lateral niche in the grave where the body is placed

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say at the grave of Lady Fatimah after her secret burial?
ai.summary: This is one of the most famous lamentations in Islamic literature, delivered by Imam ‘Ali (a) at the graveside of Lady Fatimah al-Zahra (a), the daughter of Prophet Muhammad (s), shortly after her death. The hadith describes how Fatimah asked that her illness and burial be kept secret, and that she be buried at night with her grave concealed. After burying her, ‘Ali turned toward the Prophet’s grave and poured out his grief, recounting how he had also personally prepared the Prophet for burial. He complained of the injustice done to Fatimah by the community, the usurpation of her rights and inheritance, and expressed his undying sorrow. This lamentation is a cornerstone text in Shi‘a theology regarding the events after the Prophet’s death.
